newsitem.title: USA: Boeing deal value jumps to $13.9 billion.
newsitem.headline: Boeing deal value jumps to $13.9 billion.

text.p: The indicated value of Boeing Co's proposed all-stock acquisition of McDonnell Douglas Corp rose to nearly $14 billion Monday as shares of the two aerospace companies soared.
Boeing was up 3-3/4 at 100-1/2 and McDonnell Douglas jumped 9-5/8 to 61-5/8 on the New York Stock Exchange, where they were the most active issues.
Based on the proposed ratio of 0.65 Boeing share for each McDonnell Douglas share, the deal would be worth $65.325 a share or $13.9 billion based on the company's 212.9 million shares outstanding.
Paul Gifford, director of investor relations for Boeing, said there was no "collar" on the deal that would limit the value of the proposed transaction.

Boeing officials also said two current major operating groups of the company, commercial airplanes and defense and space, would report through Harry Stonecipher, who would become president and chief operating officer of the combined company.
No other decisions have been made regarding structure of the merged company, a spokeswoman said.
